chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who drank medicine while she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that, so she miscarried her child. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had bones and flesh had grown upon them, the wergild (diyah) is upon her to be paid to his father. And if when she cast him out it was a clot (alaqah) or a lump (mudghah), then upon her is forty dinars or a ghurrah (unified price, often a slave) to be paid to his father.' I said to him, 'And she does not inherit her child's wergild along with his father?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit him.'

key_terms.عَلَقَةً: A clot of blood, an early stage of fetal development
key_terms.غُرَّةً: A unified price, often referring to a slave or a specific sum of money
key_terms.مُضْغَةً: A chewed-like lump, a subsequent stage of fetal development

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's inheritance of her miscarried child's wergild if she caused the miscarriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudence of miscarriage (tanafus) caused by medication, distinguishing compensation based on fetal development stages: a 'ghurrah' (forty dinars) for early stages and full 'diyah' for later stages, both paid to the father. It establishes the principle of 'al-dam li-ahlihi' (blood money to the heirs), explicitly excluding the mother from inheritance as the killer, a ruling consistent with Shia fiqh's application of Quranic inheritance laws to fetal compensation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who drank medicine and she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that. So her child miscarried. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there were bones for him (the child), and the flesh had grown upon him, the wergild is upon her to submit it to its father. However, if she miscarried a clot or lump (unformed), so upon her would be forty Dinars, or a slave to be paid to its father’. I said, ‘Would she not inherit the wergild of her child along with its father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, because she killed it, so she would not inherit’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from ‘Ubaydah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who takes medicine when pregnant without informing her husband, and miscarries her child. He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘If the child had grown bones and flesh then the wergild is due on her which she must pay to the father; but if the miscarriage takes place when the fetus has just formed or is an embryo she owes forty dinars or a slave to the father.’ I then asked, ‘Is it the case that she cannot inherit with the father?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She cannot inherit because she has killed the child, so she cannot inherit.’”
